primary_outcome_name: Body weight (kg) — one of three co-primary outcomes (with triceps brachii muscle thickness and push-up endurance)
primary_outcome_instrument_scale: Calibrated digital scale, 0.1 kg precision, light clothing, bladder emptied before measurement (kg)
population_detail: Healthy female university students, aged 18-26 years, with no regular resistance-training experience in the previous six months, no serious musculoskeletal/cardiovascular disorders, non-smokers/non-heavy-drinkers; recruited in Japan (Hiroshima University).

published_estimate.quote: After the intervention, eTRE had a lower weight than the control group (β = −2.92; SE = 1.00; 95% CI: [−4.88, −0.95]; p = 0.004), whereas dTRE did not differ significantly from the control (β = −0.68; SE = 1.00; 95% CI: [−2.64, 1.29]; p = 0.499). The Time × Group interaction term for eTRE (β = 2.13; SE = 0.48; 95% CI: [1.18, 3.07]; p < 0.001) indicated that eTRE experienced a significantly greater reduction in weight from pre to post compared to the control. (Section 3.3 'Changes in Body Weight', p. 6-7 of 15)

data_availability_statement: The dataset supporting this study is openly available in Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14885654.

registry_check.issues: 1) n_arms: the paper has 3 randomised arms (eTRE, dTRE, Control), not the 2 our registry row lists in arm_include. However this does NOT mean the paper only reports an omnibus 3-group test: the primary LMM used dummy-coded Group with Control as the reference category, so the paper explicitly reports a pairwise eTRE-vs-Control contrast (both a post-only simple effect, beta=-2.92, SE=1.00, 95% CI [-4.88,-0.95], p=0.004, and the Time x Group interaction/change-score contrast, beta=2.13, SE=0.48, 95% CI [1.18,3.07], p<0.001) alongside a separate dTRE-vs-Control contrast. Our registry's 2-arm subset (Control vs eTRE) is therefore a legitimate, directly-reported subset of the paper's own primary analysis, not an ad hoc contrast the paper never made. Tukey's HSD post hoc tests were additionally run across all pairwise group x time cells. 2) Body weight is only 1 of 3 co-primary outcomes declared in the Abstract ('The primary outcomes included body weight, the thickness of the triceps brachii long head..., and push-up endurance'); it is listed first among the three and is the outcome most emphasised in the Abstract/Results as the key significant finding, but no formal outcome hierarchy or multiplicity correction across the 3 co-primary outcomes is reported. 3) Deposited data naming mismatch: the Zenodo CSV 'Body data.csv' labels the delayed-TRE arm as 'mTRE', but the paper text (53 occurrences) exclusively calls it 'dTRE' -- the group is never called 'mTRE' anywhere in the manuscript. This does not affect the Control/eTRE contrast our registry uses (those labels match the paper exactly), but it is a genuine data-vs-paper naming discrepancy worth flagging for provenance. 4) Minor: registry id_var is given as 'Participant.ID' (dot) but the actual CSV column header is 'Participant-ID' (hyphen); likely harmless if read with a pipeline that sanitises names (e.g. base R read.csv), but flagged for completeness. 5) Registry outcome_var='Weight', arm_var='Group', time_var='Time', primary_time='post' all match the CSV columns/values exactly for the Control and eTRE rows.

analysis_method_quote: 2.4. Statistical Analysis ... All statistical analyses were conducted using SPSS (version 27.0, IBM Corporation, Armonk, NY, USA). The significance level was set at p < 0.05, and all results were reported as the mean ± standard deviation (mean ± SD). Due to the relatively small sample size (n = 8 per group), a linear mixed model (LMM) was employed instead of a traditional repeated-measures ANOVA to enhance the statistical power and account for individual variability. This approach allowed for a robust estimation of the within-subject and between-group effects. The dependent variables were body weight (kg), muscle thickness (mm), and push-up repetitions, with Time (pre- vs. post-intervention) and Group (eTRE, dTRE, and control) as fixed effects, along with a term for their interaction (Time × Group). In the LMM, the Group variable was dummy-coded, with the control group designated as the reference category. Participant IDs were included as random intercepts to account for individual differences. The primary focus of the analysis was the Time × Group interaction, which determined whether the changes in the dependent variables differed across groups. If a significant interaction was detected (p < 0.05), post hoc pairwise comparisons were performed using Tukey's honestly significant difference (HSD) test to identify specific group differences while adjusting for multiple comparisons. All of the models were fitted using restricted maximum likelihood estimation (REML). (Section 2.4, p. 5-6 of 15)
notes: Study: Yu & Ueda, 'Early Time-Restricted Eating Improves Weight Loss While Preserving Muscle: An 8-Week Trial in Young Women', Nutrients 2025, 17, 1022, DOI 10.3390/nu17061022, PMCID PMC11945196. Design: 3-arm parallel RCT (eTRE 8:00-14:00 window, dTRE 12:00-18:00 window, Control 8:00-20:00 window), 8 weeks, all participants performed identical supervised knee-supported push-up resistance training 3x/week; the manipulated variable across arms is exclusively the daily eating-window timing (self-implemented at home, monitored via daily phone calls/messages), not the RT protocol, which was uniform and investigator-supervised across all arms. No sample-size/power calculation is reported (paper itself flags n=24 as a limitation). Randomisation: 29 volunteers initially screened and underwent a 1-week familiarisation period; 5 withdrew during familiarisation (pre-randomisation) for training-adaptation or fasting-discomfort reasons; the remaining 24 were randomised via computer-generated sequences and sealed envelopes into 3 groups of n=8. No post-randomisation dropout is reported and Table 2 shows n=8 per arm for both pre- and post-measurements on all 3 outcomes, hence B_analysis_population coded 'itt' and B_missing_strategy 'none_missing' (all randomised participants appear analysed with complete data). No trial registration (no ClinicalTrials.gov/UMIN/other registry ID found anywhere in the text) and no separate published/registered protocol; only IRB approval (Hiroshima University Ethics Committee, HR-ES-001701) is reported, hence C_protocol_available='no' rather than 'registration_only'. journal_requires_data_sharing coded 'yes' based on MDPI's standard editorial policy of mandating a Data Availability Statement in all research articles (consistent with the DAS actually present here with a public Zenodo DOI); this is general journal-policy knowledge rather than a statement made in the paper itself. B_multiplicity coded 'other' because Tukey's HSD is explicitly used for post hoc pairwise comparisons (not one of the codebook's listed bonferroni/holm/hochberg/fdr/hierarchical options), while no correction is applied across the 3 co-primary outcomes themselves. B_baseline_handling coded 'other' (not ancova/change/endpoint) because baseline and follow-up are both modelled as levels of a within-subject Time factor inside one LMM with a Time×Group interaction, structurally a repeated-measures/longitudinal model rather than a baseline-adjusted-covariate (ANCOVA) or a pre-computed single change-score model.
